question: Check the factual claims in the report against the TCGA-BRCA release. (report: /var/folders/s3/8szxbq_97gd9h3wzx3ct9kcr0000gn/T/clearanswer_jobs/5da3143497a04b45a485a5a5262ad853/report.md)

findings.summary: Supported: 1,101 primary tumors in the release
Supported: 535 have survival, mutation, copy number, RNA and protein data
findings.claim_text: 535 have survival, mutation, copy number, RNA and protein data

findings.summary: Contradicted: Luminal A is the largest RNA subtype, accounting for about 62% of primary tumors with an RNA subtype call. Correct value: 49.9% (421 of 844 primary tumors with a PAM50Call_RNAseq call)
findings.claim_text: Luminal A is the largest RNA subtype, accounting for about 62% of primary tumors with an RNA subtype call.
findings.correct_value: 49.9% (421 of 844 primary tumors with a PAM50Call_RNAseq call)
findings.limitation: The denominator here is primary tumors with a non-null PAM50Call_RNAseq value (n=844 of 1,101 primary tumor records). The percentage changes only trivially if other denominators are used.

findings.summary: Insufficient evidence: Patients whose tumors had the highest ER-alpha protein responded best to hormone therapy
findings.claim_text: Patients whose tumors had the highest ER-alpha protein responded best to hormone therapy
findings.limitation: To verify this claim, one would need a dataset that records (a) the specific type of hormone therapy administered (e.g., tamoxifen, aromatase inhibitor), (b) a defined response endpoint (e.g., pathological complete response, recurrence-free survival on hormone therapy), and (c) ER-alpha protein/expression levels — such as data from a neoadjuvant clinical trial cohort.
